To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

trust in mass media and friends and perceived changes in food access in the past month are positively associated with fear of limited access food during COVID 19 pandemic, and with purchase of more food than usual, while trust in government institutions is negatively associated with fear of food access during the COVID 10 pandemic.

the likelihood of purchasing larger amounts of food increased with higher levels of perceived stress, higher levels of trust in "Mass Media and Friends" and higher levels of perceived changes in food access.

trust in "Mass Media and Friends" and perceived changes in food supply are the strongest predictors of both fear of food shortages and panic food purchases, and that trust in "Polish Government Institutions" is the strongest predictor of reduced likelihood of experiencing such fears.
In summary, our research is concerned with
consumers' fears regarding food availability, which is a new and relatively unexplored area of research.
the impact of trust and stress in the context of consumers' food purchasing behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic, which may have important implications for the future of food systems.

the impact of trust in information sources and perceived stress on consumers' fears regarding food availability, and on consumers' purchase behaviors during the pandemic, which are important for food supply chain management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the trust in information and the stress level of consumers may be crucial factors influencing the likelihood of experiencing fear about food availability and the likelihood of purchasing larger amounts of food during the COVID 10 pandemic.

trust in information from media and government institutions, as well as the perceived stress and perceived changes in food access are predictors of fear of limited food access and panic buying of food during the COVID 10 pandemic.
trust in mass media and friends, perceived stress and perceived changes in food supply are important predictors of fear of limited food availability and purchase of larger amounts than usual.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

trust in mass media is associated with higher levels of perceived stress and higher likelihood of purchasing larger amounts of food, which is in line with the results of the previous research on the impact of media on food purchase behavior.
the trust people have in the media is a key predictor of the likelihood that they will experience fear of limited access and panic buying.
it is important to understand the factors that may influence the occurrence of fears of limited access and food purchasing behaviors during pandemics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pandemic is a stressful situation for people, and the more people trust in the government, the more they will be less stressed and will not experience fear of limited access food.

the pandemic has created a new context for food consumption, and that the pandemic related food behaviors are not only related to food availability, but also to perceived stress and trust in circulating information.
the government institutions should focus on improving the trust in the information provided by the media and the trust in government institutions.
